title: The reserved acl.json sidecar is not repository content: no door serves, writes, deletes, moves or lists it, and a move carries the ACL entries beneath the moved node

criteria.given: any caller, through any repository door (repository resource, dashboards, apps, notebooks, history, embed-authoring, zip-upload)
criteria.then: the acl.json sidecar is never served as content and never appears in a listing; only the ACL API answers ACL questions

criteria.given: a caller without GRANT on the folder
criteria.then: writing, deleting or moving acl.json as ordinary content is refused through every door; only the ACL API (which needs GRANT) can change who owns or can read a folder or any file in it

criteria.given: a move of a node that carries ACL entries (a sidecar at or beneath it, or a per-file entry for it in its parent's sidecar)
criteria.then: the move is refused without GRANT on the source; with GRANT it succeeds and every entry is re-keyed under the new path, so files and subfolders that were PRIVATE or SECURED are still protected as before
they can still read and re-ACL their own folder, and after a permitted move the ACL lookup at the new path reports the same owner and type
it does not contain the server's absolute repository path; in particular the repository tree no longer lists acl.json (whose content is a map of absolute paths)
